title: NEB Class 11 Chemistry — Bio-inorganic Chemistry — 2024
subject: chemistry
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Discuss the biological roles of sodium, potassium, calcium, and magnesium in the human body.
questions.solution:
**Na⁺/K⁺:** the membrane pump duo — nerve impulses and fluid balance. **Ca²⁺:** bones/teeth, blood clotting, muscle contraction. **Mg²⁺:** chlorophyll's centre and cofactor for ATP enzymes.

Deficiency shows fast: cramps (Ca/Mg), irregular heartbeat (K).
questions.knowledgeNote: Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase moves 3 Na⁺ out per 2 K⁺ in — the charge gradient behind every nerve signal.

questions.question: Why is iron present in haemoglobin and magnesium in chlorophyll? What happens on deficiency?
questions.solution:
**Fe²⁺** in haem reversibly binds O₂ — oxygen transport. Deficiency → **anaemia** (low haemoglobin, fatigue).

**Mg²⁺** sits at chlorophyll's porphyrin centre, capturing light. Deficiency → **chlorosis** (yellowing leaves, failed photosynthesis).
questions.knowledgeNote: Haem and chlorophyll share the porphyrin ring — nature reuses one scaffold with different metal centres.

questions.question: What is the role of iodine in the human body? What disorder does its deficiency cause?
questions.solution:
Iodine builds the thyroid hormones T₃/T₄, which set metabolic rate and drive brain development.

Deficiency → **goitre** (enlarged thyroid) and, in pregnancy/childhood, cretinism (stunted growth, impaired intellect) — prevented by iodised salt.
questions.knowledgeNote: The Himalayan belt's historic goitre problem is why Nepal iodises all edible salt by law.

questions.question: What are metalloenzymes? Explain with the example of carbonic anhydrase.
questions.solution:
**Metalloenzymes** need a bound metal ion for catalysis.

**Carbonic anhydrase** holds Zn²⁺, which polarises water to generate OH⁻ that attacks CO₂: CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + H⁺ — running ~10⁶ turnovers/second, clearing CO₂ from blood to lungs.
questions.knowledgeNote: Removing the metal kills the enzyme — the classic test that a protein is a metalloenzyme.

questions.question: Write the harmful effects of lead and mercury on human health.
questions.solution:
**Lead:** mimics calcium — damages developing brains (lower IQ), kidneys, and red-cell synthesis; sources include old paint and batteries.

**Mercury:** attacks the nervous system (tremors, Minamata disease); methylmercury bioaccumulates up food chains into fish.
questions.knowledgeNote: Both are cumulative poisons with no safe threshold in children — chelation therapy is the clinical response.

questions.question: What is the role of cobalt in the human body? Name its vitamin.
questions.solution:
Cobalt is the metal centre of **vitamin B₁₂ (cobalamin)**, essential for red-cell formation and nerve myelination.

Deficiency → pernicious anaemia — historically treated with liver, now with B₁₂ supplements.
questions.knowledgeNote: B₁₂ is the only vitamin with a metal atom — and the only one plants cannot make, hence vegan supplementation.
